LESSON: WRITING 6.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING: PICTORIAL COMPOSITION

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.4: Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition, part of Strand 6 in Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we enjoy looking at pictures? 2. What messages do pictures communicate?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. interpret pictures collaboratively with peers,

2. match the pictures with the different parts of a composition: beginning, middle and end,

3. watch a variety of pictorial compositions collaboratively with peers,

4. arrange different pictures logically to write a story coherently,

5. write a pictorial composition of about 120 -160 words,

6. proof read the pictorial composition,

7. display their compositions in the classroom. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. interpret pictures collaboratively with peers,
2. match the pictures with the different parts of a composition: beginning, middle and end,
3. watch a variety of pictorial compositions collaboratively with peers,
4. arrange different pictures logically to write a story coherently,
5. write a pictorial composition of about 120 -160 words,
6. proof read the pictorial composition,
7. display their compositions in the classroom. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 6.4.1 Creative Writing: Pictorial Composition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration is enhanced as the learner works with peers to watch a variety of pictorial

compositions.

• Creativity and Imagination is nurtured as the learner interprets pictures and writes stories.

Values:
Responsibility is achieved as the learner takes up assigned roles of creating and proofreading pictorial compositions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skill Education: Effective communication is enhanced as the learner expresses themselves in writing a pictorial

composition of about 120 -160 words.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can apply the skills to similar concepts in Art and Craft drawing, and Social Studies which features

interpretation of maps and charts.
